clue.text: Raise trophy, top prize

parts.note: to jack something up is to raise it
a pot is slang for a sporting trophy or cup

explanation.surface: A winner lifts the cup after taking the biggest award on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: The biggest prize in a lottery or game is called this, so it is the top award.

clue.text: Record banter about old lady's long coat

indicators.note: the banter word goes round the record

parts.note: to josh is to tease or banter
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Chatter about recording an old woman's long coat.
explanation.definitionFit: An eighteenth-century woman's long riding coat was called by this name.

clue.text: Singer keen to collect articles

indicators.note: the cry word gathers the articles inside it

parts.note: to keen is to wail or cry
AN and A are the indefinite articles

explanation.surface: A singer is eager to gather some pieces for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keen' looks like eager but is the verb meaning to wail.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow bird is kept for its song, so it is a singer.

clue.text: Present courses altered to cover rare ancestors

parts.note: PR is a grammar abbreviation for present

indicators.note: the reshuffled letters wrap round the letter for rare
altered says the letters of courses are changed into a different order

explanation.surface: Revised courses now cover rare forebears in the curriculum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift or the here and now, but here it is the grammar abbreviation (as in present tense).
explanation.definitionFit: Forerunners who came before someone are their predecessors, much as ancestors precede descendants.

clue.text: Fan of Queen's inspiring European books

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the tom word takes the letter inside

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, so a tomcat would be her admirer; with 's this gives toms

explanation.surface: A Queen fan's record collection includes a European volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests the rock band, but it is a female cat, whose admirer is a tom.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomes are large, weighty books.

clue.text: Swim at the weir? Some guy has dived in

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a swim at the weir is on, since a man has already plunged in.
explanation.walkthrough: The man's name sits inside 'swiM AT THE Weir', diving into the words just as the surface's swimmer dives into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male first name, so it fits a man who has plunged into the phrase.

clue.text: Pick this row after staff function

indicators.note: after places the row word behind the other two

parts.note: to staff a post is to man it
a do is a party or function
a line is a row

explanation.surface: Choose this line of seats behind the staff party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick' looks like choose, but a mandoline is plucked with a plectrum, or pick.
explanation.definitionFit: This stringed instrument is played with a plectrum, a small pick, so you pick it.

clue.text: Row after mother's abandoned dog

indicators.note: abandoned means the mother's letters are dropped from the dog

parts.note: a mastiff is a large breed of dog
ma's, mother's, gives MAS

explanation.surface: An argument follows when Mum's dog is left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a minor quarrel, the sense of row that rhymes with cow.

clue.text: Priest's greeting irregular, ignoring a rector

parts.note: hi is a greeting

indicators.note: ignoring means one letter for rector is left out of the word for irregular

parts.note: erratic means irregular
R abbreviates rector

explanation.surface: A priest says hello oddly, snubbing a rector.
explanation.definitionFit: Hieratic means of or relating to priests, so it works as the possessive adjective.

clue.text: Spivs start to wilfully disobey criminal

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
criminal suggests the letters are bent out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: Black-market dealers begin to break the law on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: A spiv is British slang for a flashy petty crook or black-market trader.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide boys are British slang for sharp, petty crooks, the same type as spivs.

clue.text: Understand notice Poles brought in

indicators.note: the poles are carried inside the word for notice

parts.note: to notice something is to see it
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: A briefing on grasping a notice once Polish workers have been brought into the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: To make sense of something is to understand it; the verb sense means grasp or perceive.

clue.text: Kiwi who wrote manuscript about an area

indicators.note: the manuscript letters go round the word an

parts.note: a field is an area of land

explanation.surface: A New Zealand author's handwritten draft concerns a particular stretch of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kiwi' is a New Zealander here, not the bird or the fruit: Katherine Mansfield was born in Wellington.
explanation.definitionFit: Katherine Mansfield, the short-story writer, was a New Zealander, which is what Kiwi means colloquially.

clue.text: Camp comic operas in US

indicators.note: comic suggests the words are made ridiculous and jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A camp style of comic opera is staged in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camp' looks like flamboyant theatre but means a faction or side, as in a political camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A persuasion is a group sharing one belief, just as a camp is a faction holding a common view.

clue.text: A little bit of William Blake

definitions.text: A little bit of William Blake

indicators.note: only a small piece of the poet's name is taken, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A short extract from the poet William Blake.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'wilLIAM Blake', and the result is itself a small unit of a poet's verse.
explanation.definitionFit: This metrical foot of one short and one long syllable is a tiny building block of verse, such as Blake wrote.

clue.text: Bargain over attempts to import power suits

indicators.note: over says the bargain word is turned back to front

parts.note: a snip is a bargain

indicators.note: the attempts word takes the power letter inside

parts.note: tries are attempts
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Haggling over attempts to bring in powerful business wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power suits' reads as one phrase, but 'power' gives P and 'suits' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinstripes are suits with thin stripes, a classic look in city offices.

clue.text: In old age, sister conceivably shows taste

indicators.note: the sibling word goes inside the word for old age

parts.note: senility is the frailty of old age
a sister is one example of a sib, a sibling, hence conceivably

explanation.surface: An elderly sister, perhaps, still displays refined judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensibility is refined feeling and discernment, close to good taste in art or manners.

clue.text: New uni lecturer told story about fine I revoked

parts.note: U abbreviates university

indicators.note: the lying word goes round the fine letter and I

parts.note: to tell a story is to lie
F abbreviates fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A new university lecturer invented a tale about a penalty being cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: To nullify is to cancel or make void, so revoked is a close synonym.

clue.text: Stuck page in book to finish exam

parts.note: the end is the finish
an exam is a paper

explanation.surface: A student stuck on a page of a textbook must still finish the test.
explanation.definitionFit: An endpaper is the sheet pasted inside a book's cover, glued to the board.

clue.text: Novices run twice in different parts of US

indicators.note: the two run letters go into separate places in the country word
twice means the run letter is used two times

parts.note: the US is the United States
R abbreviates run in cricket scores

explanation.surface: Beginners run two times in various regions of America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in different parts of' means the two run letters go in at separate places, not side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Starters are those just beginning something, so beginners or novices.

clue.text: Note Scottish water's wholesome quality

parts.note: a natural is a musical note neither sharp nor flat
Loch Ness is a famous Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A musical score remarks on the healthy character of water from Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unaffected and unprocessed is a wholesome trait, which this abstract noun names.

clue.text: Book addict keeps one working harder

indicators.note: keeps means the addict word holds the letter inside

parts.note: a user is a drug addict
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A bookish addict retains one job and works more.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone busier is more occupied, so working harder than before.

clue.text: In which to display Ceres bust society collected?

definitions.text: In which to display Ceres bust society collected?

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the goddess's name is broken into a new order

explanation.surface: Where would a society put the sculpted bust of the goddess Ceres it acquired?
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' is both the sculpture in the surface and the anagram signal for CERES.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove set into a wall is a classic place to stand a statue or bust for display.

clue.text: Position pawn next to a queen and king

parts.note: P is the chess abbreviation for pawn
R, for Regina, stands for a queen
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A chess move: set the pawn down beside the queen and king.
explanation.definitionFit: To park something is to put it in a place and leave it, so to position it.

clue.text: Blow is from turbulent air

indicators.note: turbulent means stirred up, so these letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: A gust comes out of churning air, as in a weather report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' seems to be wind, given the turbulent air, but means a setback.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow is a sudden piece of bad luck or a setback, which is what this misfortune means.

clue.text: Liberated female does get upset

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down clue the word is written upwards

parts.note: does are female deer

explanation.surface: A released female deer becomes agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: Freed means released or set at liberty, the same as liberated.

clue.text: Cuddle old writer

parts.note: a hug is a cuddle

explanation.surface: Embrace an elderly author.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor Hugo was the French novelist who wrote Les Misérables.

clue.text: Prince and English duke admitted to fuel damage

indicators.note: the duke's letter is let inside the word for fuel

parts.note: juice is slang for petrol or electricity, a fuel

explanation.surface: Royals letting a duke near the petrol leads to harm.
explanation.definitionFit: To prejudice a case or someone's chances is to harm them, so it means damage as a verb.

clue.text: Lions free to stop training

indicators.note: the word for free plugs the middle of the training letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, gym training
to rid is to free of something

explanation.surface: Big cats are released so they cannot be trained any more.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of lions is called this, the collective noun for the animals.

clue.text: Counter drones flying over centre of airport

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters are sent off into a new order
the middle letter of airport is taken

explanation.surface: Defence systems counter drones flying over the middle of an airport.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of 'airport' is P; with DRONES it is shuffled as one pool.
explanation.definitionFit: To counter a remark is to reply to it, to answer back.

clue.text: Courses cleared of small leaves

indicators.note: one letter for small is removed from the courses word

parts.note: desserts are courses of a meal

explanation.surface: Plates are cleared of the last small salad leaves between courses.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert is to abandon or go away from, which is what leaves means as a verb here.
